Bootstrap Variance of a Fit

Source: R/bootstrap_objects.R
bootstrap_vcov.Rd

Selects the variance that is the covariance of the coefficients of refitted, resampled data sets. The matrix is not read from the curvature at the mode: it is the empirical covariance of the replicates that add_bootstrap() stores in the fit.

Usage

bootstrap_vcov(n = NULL, resample = NULL, refit = NULL, cores = 1)

Arguments

n

A single whole number, the total number of replicates, or NULL.

resample

A resample_method object, or NULL.

refit

"coefficients", "full" or NULL.

cores

The number of separate R processes over which replicates that have to be computed at the call are refitted, a single whole number (default 1). It is distinct from the threads of statmod(), which counts threads inside one process. The values of the replicates do not depend on it.

Value

A BootstrapVcov object, inheriting from vcov_method, with the property name equal to "bootstrap" and the properties n, resample, refit and cores.

Details

The arguments that are NULL are resolved against the replicates stored in the fit. A NULL argument takes the value of the stored entry if exactly one entry matches the arguments that were given, and the default otherwise (n = 200, parametric_resample(), "coefficients"). If several entries match, an error prints the table of entries. A setting that matches no stored entry is computed at the call and stored in the fit, with a message that says how many replicates were computed. n is the total that is wanted: with an entry of \(m\) replicates, \(n > m\) computes the \(n - m\) missing ones, and \(n \le m\) uses the first \(n\) without computing anything. summary.StatmodFit() and confint.StatmodFit() resolve the variance once, so the replicates are computed once.

The coordinates are those of vcov.StatmodFit(): the coefficients of every equation, with the aliased ones missing. A coefficient under a kinked penalty (modelterms7::lasso(), modelterms7::scad(), modelterms7::mcp()) that the fit holds at zero has a variance here, which includes the mass of the replicates at zero, where the other conventions report it as missing. With readable = TRUE the readable quantities are computed for each replicate and the covariance is taken afterwards.

The variance estimates the sampling variance of the penalized estimator. It does not contain the smoothing bias that bayesian_vcov() carries as variance, so an interval around a penalized term built from it covers less than the nominal level, as one built from frequentist_vcov() does. With refit = "coefficients" the hyperparameters are held at the values of the fit, and the matrix is a relative of frequentist_vcov(). With refit = "full" the hyperparameters are selected again on every replicate, and the variability of the hyperparameters enters; it costs about ten times more. The relative Monte Carlo error of a standard error is about \(1/\sqrt{2n}\). A replicate that fails (an error, a mode error above mode_error_limit(), a coefficient that is not identified) is replaced; replacing conditions the bootstrap on success, which understates the variability when failures are frequent.

The convention has no information argument: the matrix is not built from the information. The refits use the inner_information of the fit.

See also

add_bootstrap(), which computes and stores the replicates, statmod_bootstrap(), which reads them, and vcov_method.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(60))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(60, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
bootstrap_vcov()
#> <vcov> bootstrap (n as stored, resample as stored, refit as stored)
fit <- add_bootstrap(fit, n = 40, resample = case_resample())
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit, vcov_type = bootstrap_vcov())))
#>    mu:(Intercept)              mu:x sigma:(Intercept) 
#>         0.1263922         0.1736775         0.1165450 
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
#>    mu:(Intercept)              mu:x sigma:(Intercept) 
#>        0.09832324        0.17020018        0.09284767
